messages:
maria: quick sync — followup on the tenant routing boundary convergence RFC. goal: pick a single long-term pattern and a low-risk migration path. two options we debated: per-tenant gateway (full isolation) vs regional shared gateway with tenant routing slices. thoughts?

raj: my quick read — per-tenant gateway gives strongest isolation and easiest cert/egress mapping, but ops cost and IP exhaustion risk. shared gateway is cheaper but complexity spikes (routing rules, per-tenant quotas, src-ip preservation is trickier).

ben: agree with raj. also: shared gateway forces us to enhance the controlplane->dataplane contract for tenant affinity and fallback. we currently have a simple "tenant_id" header, but routing slices need a richer handshake (desired egress IP, preferred zone, cert thumbprints).

alexa: +1. question: do we need per-tenant outbound IP preservation for compliance customers? if yes, per-tenant gateway is almost mandatory unless we add SNAT mapping state to shared gateway.

maria: for compliance customers we'll keep reserved egress pools, but the goal is default pattern for most customers. leaning toward shared gateway with an operator-managed per-tenant override (i.e., we run regional shared gateways but can carve dedicated gateways for flagged tenants).

raj: that hybrid sounds reasonable. migration-wise we can start with: 1) extend connector handshake to report desired properties, 2) implement routing-slice controller in controlplane, 3) route new tenants to shared gateway by default, 4) provide a migration tool for existing dedicated tenants to opt-in to shared slices.

ben: technical nit: the connector handshake extension needs versioning. we should introduce a stable "routing.contract.v1" payload and leave room for v2. also need idempotent apply semantics.

alexa: agree on versioning. also add a graceful fallback: if shared gateway loses lease or caps out, connectors should fall back to a compatible model (dedicated gateway or regional fallback) — define explicit error codes so SDKs can surface them.

maria: good point. add an automated canary: route 5% of new tenants to shared slices for the first 2 weeks, observability for latency and dst-ip churn. if regressions > threshold, pause.

raj: ops concerns: IP exhaustion. propose an allocator that pre-reserves /28 blocks per slice with burst borrowing across regions. we need soft quotas and emergency reserve pool for enterprise.

ben: and telemetry — add token-level egress mapping metrics and per-tenant NAT churn. we'll want to correlate request ids to egress IP changes in the console.

alexa: auth/certs: for shared gateways, we can centralize TLS termination but must support SNI passthrough for tenant certs in some enterprise flows. that adds complexity for autoscaling.

maria: summary action items:
- maria: draft an operator playbook for carving dedicated gateways (due EOD Fri)
- raj: design the routing.contract.v1 payload and edge controller API (spike by Tue)
- ben: add egress-mapping telemetry fields + dashboard mock (PR by next Wed)
- alexa: spec SNI passthrough constraints + perf implications (doc by Mon)

raj: +1 on deadlines. also: we should sketch a rollback plan if shared gateway incurs higher p99 latency — maybe automated route reversion to dedicated pool per-tenant.

maria: yes. also add a small integration test: simulate 10k connectors with mixed desired-egress to ensure allocator scales.

infra-bot: deployment notice: rolling deploy of routing-slice-controller to staging started (build ci-4823) — 1718523500

ben: saw the deploy notice. will hook the new telemetry fields into the test cluster.

alexa: small config snippet for the routing.contract.v1 I sketched earlier:
```json
{
  "version": "routing.contract.v1",
  "tenant_id": "t-1234",
  "egress_policy": {
    "preferred_ips": ["reserve:enterprise-1"],
    "preserve_srcip": true
  },
  "affinity": {
    "zone_hint": "us-west-2",
    "fallback": "regional-shared"
  }
}
```

maria: perfect — that captures the fields we discussed. make sure the controller validates preferred_ips against the allocator ledger.

raj: one more: network ACLs and DNS split-horizon. shared gateway needs to push tenant-specific DNS overrides for private endpoints. that'll be part of the routing-slice controller responsibilities.

ben: could we keep DNS pushes idempotent by using a version stamp on each tenant's override set? controller compares stamp and only applies diffs. avoids flapping.

alexa: +1. also ensure we don't leak tenant zones when pushing shared gateway configs (mask highly privileged fields).

maria: OK team, this feels like a convergent plan: default shared gateway + carve-outs, contract v1, allocator with reserve pool, telemetry and canary. I'll update the RFC with these outcomes and the action list. thanks. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: staging rollout complete for routing-slice-controller (ci-4823) — 1718523555

ben: running the scale test now, will post results in this thread.

maria: thanks — keep updates here, and we can sync next Tue for design review.
